item.title: 2027: Amupitan assures INEC workers of improved welfare, remuneration
item.description: The National Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has assured its staff members of improved welfare and remuneration ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the assurance while addressing INEC Staff in the South-East on preparedness for the 2027 General Elections in Enugu on Monday. The chairman came on a working visit to interact with traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders of the South-East. He urged the staff to steer clear of partisan politics, adding: “You should not pick interest in any political party: be neutral and firm”. “I am hearing that some of you are showing interest in some political parties. This is absolutely wrong. “The commission wants you to be neutral and professional both in your words and actions. “The commission will not take unprofessional or unethical electoral conduct from any staff. “We have instituted a reward and sanction mechanism at local government area, state and to even national level,” he said. The chairman said that the commission was working relentlessly to improve the welfare of its staff across all cadres and levels. He claimed that the commission had worked hard to remove its staff from the normal civil service salary structure to a special salary structure. “This new special salary structure will take effect from Jan. 1, 2027 and it is for the benefit of staff across all cadres and levels. “We want the new salary structure so that you will not be easily induced by anybody before, during and after the elections. “We are working with other relevant governmental agencies and commissions to make the cash backing for the new salary structure possible,” he said He urged all staff to ensure that they returned the trust of the people to the commission’s programmes and activities. “As an unbiased umpire, we need to up the confidence and trust the people repose on us by being disciplined and diligent to our duties at all times,” he said. Amupitan also said the commission was making provisions for logistics and had already given INEC Enugu office 10 new pick-up vans. “More logistics are coming as we ensure adequate preparation for the general elections. “We have got our non-sensitive materials ready; while we are awarding contracts for other materials needed in the election as well as sensitive materials as well. “Massive training and retraining will commence soon and the retraining is imperative given new guidelines and regulations introduced into the Amended Electoral Act,” he added. item.title: Saudi Arabia executes Bangladeshi newlyweds over mosque kiss
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Two Bangladeshi nationals, identified as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siri Akhtar, have reportedly been executed in Saudi Arabia following their conviction over an alleged immoral act inside a mosque in Mecca. Reports circulating on social media and seen by Vanguard showed that Bangladesh claimed the couple, who had travelled to Mecca for their honeymoon, were accused of kissing on the forehead inside the mosque. The gesture was reportedly an expression of gratitude to Allah for their marriage. The reports further claimed that the couple’s bodies had been returned to Bangladesh in two coffins for burial. item.title: NAF airstrike kills ISWAP leaders in Lake Chad
item.description: The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has neutralised key figures of the Islamic State of West Africa Province (ISWAP) in a precision air strike in the Lake Chad region. This is contained in a statement by the Director, Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, on Monday in Abuja. Ejodame said the operation was conducted under the Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), on an identified terrorist hideout on Monday. He said the operation underscored the NAF’s sustained commitment to degrading terrorist networks, disrupting their logistics and enhancing security in the North-East. According to him, preliminary post-strike assessments indicate that several prominent ISWAP fighters were neutralised. He revealed that those neutralised include key figures within the group’s security structure and leadership council, like Jindullah, the Chief Security Guard and confidant of Abu Saleem, as well as Abul Kissa, a member of ISWAP Shura Council. Ejodame said the strike also destroyed logistical assets including boat engines and motorcycles believed to support the group’s movement and operational activities. “The operation demonstrates the NAF’s intense effort to conduct intelligence-led precision strikes against terrorist enclaves concealed within difficult terrain. “By neutralising key operatives and destroying critical logistical resources, the strike delivers a significant setback to ISWAP’s operational capability, further constraining its ability to coordinate activities and threaten vulnerable communities,” he said. The NAF spokesman quoted the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, as reaffirming the NAF’s resolve to sustain decisive air operations against terrorist networks. Aneke said the operations were in support of ongoing efforts to restore peace and stability across the country. item.title: ‘I’m very proud of you’ — Tinubu showers praise on CityBoy Movement
item.description: By Bayo Wahab President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday praised the City Boy Movement for what he described as a new model of political organisation in Nigeria, telling its members he was “very proud” of them. The President spoke at the State House during a ceremonial meeting with the group and the Relax Tinubu is Fixing Nigeria (RTIFN) support group. Addressing members of the movement, Tinubu said the group had introduced something new to the country’s politics by going beyond mobilising crowds. “The CityBoy Movement, to all of you, you have done something new in Nigeria politics. You did not just gather people; you built a structure, millions of real, verifiable members,” the President said. He highlighted the group’s national spread, noting that it has “a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling units.” The President also commended the movement’s engagement with young people, citing its call centre and its community outreach programme, CityBoy Care. “You drilled down; a call center that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listen to whatever their community needs. CityBoy Care, meeting members where they live,” he said. Tinubu described the group’s approach as organised and purposeful, rather than the product of mere publicity. “That is not noise. That is organisation. That is excellent thinking. That is the kind of seriousness this country needs from its young people, and I’m very proud of you. I must say so,” he said. The President also thanked members for defending his administration publicly, including at moments when doing so carried a political cost. “You were patient when patience was hard. You defended this administration in the market, on the campuses, at the motorparks and on social media even when it was not popular to do so,” Tinubu said. He added that their loyalty had not gone unnoticed. “I saw it, I noticed, and I will never forget it. I say thank you once again,” the President said. The City Boy Movement was founded by the President’s son, Seyi Tinubu, who is also its patron. item.title: Saudi postpones top investment conference to 2027 after Houthi attacks
item.description: A major Saudi investment conference has been postponed to next year, its chief executive officer said on Monday, as the kingdom comes under repeated attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. The annual Future Investment Initiative (FII), often dubbed “Davos in the Desert”, was scheduled to take place from October 26-29. For nearly a decade, it has served as a showcase for Saudi Arabia’s efforts to attract global investors, business leaders and heads of state. The postponement deals a blow to the kingdom’s ambitions to draw foreign capital, diversify its oil-reliant economy and push its reform agenda. In a statement posted on X, FII Institute CEO Maha Al Saud said the gathering would instead take place in 2027, saying organisers wanted to ensure the anniversary edition delivered the “full scale” and “extraordinary quality” expected by participants. She said new dates would be announced soon, while current registrations and partnerships would remain valid. Three sources familiar with the matter had earlier told AFP the conference would be postponed. One source said organisers “won’t announce a new date soon” while another questioned who would be willing to “risk flying to Riyadh these days”. The decision comes after Riyadh’s international airport, a repeated target of Houthi attacks, suspended operations earlier this month after 13 people were killed in an October 10 strike, with no clear timeline for when air traffic could resume. It was the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade. Earlier this month, diplomatic sources said the kingdom was planning to move ahead with the conference, offering on-site and virtual attendance, as well as alternative air and land travel routes. But that plan appears to have been scrapped as Western travel warnings for the region have multiplied and the airport remains shut. “The executives I’ve spoken to are very, very, very hesitant to travel to Riyadh for this month’s conferences,” a consultant who advises Saudi firms told AFP. “Companies won’t put their employees in harm’s way for the sake of an investment conference,” they added. item.title: Trump to Netanyahu: You’ll have ‘tremendous’ election win
item.description: US President Donald Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday he expected him to win a “tremendous” election victory next week, with the Israeli leader suggesting they may again attack Iran together. A day after Trump publicly endorsed Netanyahu in the close-fought October 27 election, the Israeli premier put out a video of the two right-wing leaders lavishing praise on each other by telephone. “I think you’re going to have a tremendous victory, actually,” Trump can be heard saying, with Netanyahu putting his mobile on speakerphone. “You’re the man I want by my side, Bibi,” Trump said, referring to Netanyahu by his nickname. Netanyahu — while reminding the famously loose-lipped president that they were on an open line — hailed Trump for joining Israel in attacking Iran, a decades-long goal of Israel’s longest-serving prime minister. “Donald, we have a job to finish,” Netanyahu said. “We’ll finish it together. We’ll finish it, and no one else will do it.” Netanyahu did not elaborate but again described Iran’s clerical state, which remains in power nearly eight months after the joint massive attack, as “the greatest danger”. item.title: Tompolo mourns Uduaghan, hails role in Niger Delta peace
item.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire, Warri Chairman of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has mourned former Delta State Governor Emmanuel Uduaghan, crediting him with contributing to peace in the Niger Delta. Tompolo, in a condolence statement issued by his media consultant, Dr Paul Bebenimibo, on Monday, said Uduaghan played a significant role during the peak of militancy in the oil-producing region. He recalled the former governor’s support for the Presidential Amnesty Programme and the pipeline surveillance arrangement introduced during the administrations of late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and former President Goodluck Jonathan. The statement said Tompolo received news of Uduaghan’s death with sadness, adding that he did not expect the announcement at this time. It read, “Tompolo recalled the role of the former governor during the days of militancy in the Niger Delta; how the former governor supported the Presidential Amnesty Programme and the pipeline surveillance job awarded during the time of late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and former President Goodluck Jonathan.” The Tantita chairman described Uduaghan’s death as a great loss and said the former governor would be greatly missed. He also prayed to God to give the deceased’s family and other mourners the strength to bear the loss. item.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, has agreed to appear on Nigerian content creator Bae U Barbie’s YouTube programme, Curiosity Made Me Ask, following an invitation to engage younger audiences. Bae U Barbie, born Adebayo Ridwan, extended the invitation while questioning the billionaire about his media engagements and the need to reach young Nigerians interested in his business and its planned initial public offering (IPO). The content creator observed that most of Dangote’s interviews had been conducted on platforms that were not popular among younger audiences, despite their interest in investing in his company. “Most of the interviews we’ve seen you have been on platforms that my generation don’t watch,” Bae U Barbie said in a video posted on social media on Monday. He clarified that he was not asking Dangote to dismiss his media team but urged the businessman to consider appearing on his show after completing his existing engagements. “I’m not saying you should sack your media team. No, but you know, when you finish,” he said before asking when the billionaire would feature on the programme. Responding, Dangote acknowledged the importance of engaging younger Nigerians, describing them as the country’s future while admitting that his generation had not done enough for Nigeria and Africa. “Honestly, the future that we have is actually you, the youth. We, our own generation, really, we have not really done very well for Nigeria and also for Africa. That’s the truth,” he said. The billionaire stressed the need for older Nigerians to share their experiences with younger people to help them understand the country’s history and development. “So we need to sit down with some of you and discuss our own experience with you,” he added. item.title: Troops rescue 11 passengers, foil kidnap attempt in Kogi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 12 Composite Brigade of the Nigerian Army have foiled a kidnapping attempt and rescued 11 passengers along Kabba-Ayere Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the incident occurred on October 18, 2026. He said troops deployed at the patrol base in Kabba were on routine patrol when they responded to credible intelligence about suspected terrorists attempting to abduct passengers travelling in a commercial vehicle along the route. “On arrival, the troops made contact with the terrorists and engaged them, forcing them to abandon the victims and flee into the surrounding bush,” he said. Abdullahi said nine passengers, including the driver, were rescued during the initial operation. He added that the driver and two other passengers who sustained injuries were evacuated for medical attention, while the commercial vehicle was handed over to the appropriate authorities. According to him, troops conducted a follow-up operation on October 19, 2026, during which they searched the area and rescued two additional passengers who had fled into the bush during the encounter. The operation brought the total number of rescued passengers to 11. Abdullahi said the operation underscored the brigade’s commitment to protecting lives and property, denying terrorists freedom of action and improving the safety of commuters across Kogi State. He urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing operations. The Nigerian Army, he added, remained committed to sustaining efforts to safeguard lives and property and ensure the security of residents of Kogi State. item.title: ‘It’s easier you put me in prison than take my phone away’ — Dangote
item.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote has said he would rather be imprisoned than have his phone taken away, describing losing access to the device as a “no-go area”. Dangote made the remark at an event in Lagos where he unveiled his “Vision 2030” plan for Africa’s industrial revolution. During the event, the billionaire businessman was asked to choose between spending one week without his phone or giving up access to his private jet. Responding to the question, Dangote said he would find it more difficult to part with his phone than his private jet. “Ah… I think it’s easier you put me in prison than to take my phone away. So, you know, I mean taking my phone away is no-go area, okay?” The industrialist also revealed that he has more than 13,000 contacts saved on his phone, highlighting the importance of the device in maintaining his extensive network of personal and professional relationships. “I know that would be almost… my number — I have that number since… Twitter… I have more than 13,000 contacts on my phone.” Reacting to the size of his contact list, Dangote added that he rarely blocks people, suggesting that this has contributed to the large number of contacts on his device. “Wow. Wow. I hardly… I don’t like blocking people, so a lot of people” His comments offer a glimpse into how the billionaire uses his phone to maintain connections, even as he oversees business interests spanning manufacturing, cement, fertiliser, oil refining and other sectors across Africa. Dangote is the president and chief executive of Dangote Group, one of Africa’s largest industrial conglomerates. item.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension after Portugal camp walkout
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension for leaving the Portuguese national team camp during the UEFA Nations League, the country’s football federation (FPF) announced on Monday. The 41-year-old left the Portugal camp on September 30, before accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed. The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star, who will also have to pay a fine of 255 euros ($286), has received the minimum penalty provided for in the federation’s regulations, which stipulate suspensions of between one and six months for leaving the national team. Ronaldo left Portugal’s squad after first being made to warm up as a substitute against Norway on September 27 and not brought on, and then finding out he would not start against Denmark in the match on October 1. Ronaldo’s suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will complete it by the end of October. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is Portugal’s all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker. But in his absence, Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare. Portugal host Denmark on November 14 and then travel to face Wales on November 17 in their final two Nations League Group A4 matches — by which time Ronaldo will have served his suspension. The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account “the remorse shown in the statement” issued by Ronaldo on October 6, in which he admitted his mistake and expressed his willingness to accept a punishment. The TSC is a statutory charge meant to be shared among aviation agencies (NCAA, NAMA, NiMet, NSIB and NCAT) for safety oversight, training and the proper functioning of the sector. “A more debilitating assault on the psyche of agency workers, who are our union members, is that the non-remittance of the TSC has rendered the implementation of the various duly negotiated collective bargaining agreements of the agencies nugatory, and agitated staff were becoming uncontrollable. This was seen as an accident waiting to happen. “To avoid a total shutdown of Nigerian airspace at once and in the interest of the travelling public, the joint unions strategically resolved to picket the defaulting airlines sequentially, one after the other, each day. Air Peace Airlines was scheduled for August 11, 2026. “The picketing was peaceful, lawful and conducted at the airline’s operational office/counter area, not on the airside. During the barricades, staff of Air Peace also became physically violent against unarmed union members performing their lawful trade union duties. They incited passengers against the union members, but the unions conducted themselves decorously, remaining unprovoked and undeterred. “The action was, however, suspended on the afternoon of the first day following the welcome intervention of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the security agencies at the airport. “In reaction to the lawful picketing, Air Peace Airlines became frustrated that other defaulting airlines were allowed to operate that day. item.title: ADC campaign knocks Oyedele over ₦4,000/$ fuel subsidy warning
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Director of Media and Publicity of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, has challenged the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, to publish the economic model behind his warning that a return to fuel subsidy could push the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar. Ologbondiyan accused the Federal Government of using fear to discourage debate on fuel subsidy, insisting that Nigerians deserve evidence, not alarming projections, on the potential economic consequences of restoring the policy. Speaking to Vanguard, he described the minister’s warning as scaremongering and demanded that the government explain how it arrived at the projected exchange rate. “The Minister of Finance is merely scaremongering. He cannot claim that a return to fuel subsidy will cause the naira to depreciate to ₦4,000 to the dollar without showing Nigerians the model behind that projection,” he said. Ologbondiyan questioned the reliance on investors’ concerns to oppose a subsidy return, challenging the government to identify those behind the projections and disclose their calculations. “They should show Nigerians who is making these claims and explain how they arrived at an exchange rate of ₦4,000 to the dollar if fuel subsidy is reintroduced,” he said. He also argued that Nigeria was not the only country to consider or operate a production subsidy, maintaining that the proposal should be assessed on its economic merits rather than dismissed through dire forecasts. “I do not believe this projection is realistic. It is fantasy,” he said. Oyedele had warned that a return to fuel subsidy could send the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar, while also raising concerns about investors’ perception of the opposition. Other targets include more than tripling corporate bond issuance as a share of GDP, increasing sukuk market penetration from 0.3 per cent to at least five per cent of GDP, and raising pension assets from six per cent to 16 per cent of GDP. Oyedele said Nigeria was also working to improve its standing among international investors, citing the country’s reinstatement in the FTSE Russell Frontier Market Index on September 21, 2026, and the inclusion of Nigerian government bonds in a new J.P. Morgan government bond index, with a weight of 7.4 per cent. He said the government was seeking a return to J.P. Morgan’s flagship government bond index and an eventual upgrade to emerging-market status. The minister added that the government was targeting an investment-grade credit rating within three years, noting that this would require sustained reforms, improved market liquidity and reliable repatriation of foreign investors’ funds. As part of efforts to deepen domestic investment, Oyedele formally launched the National Savings Scheme, designed to provide Nigerians with regulated avenues to save and invest towards education, housing, business development and retirement. He said the scheme would offer accessible investment channels, transparent information, reasonable costs and a functional complaints process, with tax incentives provided within the law. Oyedele expressed concern that many young Nigerians were investing their money in betting platforms, unregulated cryptocurrency schemes and Ponzi schemes instead of regulated investment products. He said the scheme would help channel domestic savings into productive investments, including through small contributions made using mobile phones. The minister also announced plans to strengthen enforcement against Ponzi schemes through improved surveillance, social media monitoring and collaboration with law enforcement agencies. He added that the government was considering a fraud restitution mechanism to support victims. Speaking at the conference, SEC Director-General Dr Emomotimi Agama said the master plan was designed to deepen market participation, expand investment products and strengthen the integrity and infrastructure of the capital market. He disclosed that a Project Steering Committee and a Capital Market Master Plan Implementation Committee would be inaugurated to oversee implementation. “Every commitment in NCMMP 2.0 will have an owner, a timeline and a scorecard, and we will report progress openly to this nation,” he said. Agama said equity market capitalisation crossed ₦100 trillion for the first time in January and rose above ₦160 trillion in September, while the All-Share Index gained about 60 per cent in 2026, following a 51 per cent return in 2025. However, he warned that the increase in market value had not been matched by sufficient participation among Nigerians, noting that too few citizens owned shares, bonds or units in collective investment schemes. “The strength of any capital market rests on the savings of its people.
